title: Fastest Guess-and-Determine Attack on Three-Round AES
summary: A solution faster than exhaustive search was found for three-round AES, but the fastest attack in the considered guess-and-determine class remains unknown.

formal_statement.body: Determine $\min_{A\in\mathcal{G}_{3\mathrm{R}}}T(A)$, where $\mathcal{G}_{3\mathrm{R}}$ is the considered guess-and-determine class.

scope.domain: Automated cryptanalysis of three-round AES via guess-and-determine attack search.
parameters: G_3R: the considered guess-and-determine class for the three-round target
T(A): the objective value minimized over candidate attacks
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the minimum objective value over the considered class, thereby resolving which three-round AES attack is fastest within that class.

citations.label: Automatic Search of Attacks on Round-Reduced AES and Applications

progress.summary: The source reports that exhaustive search was completed through 2.5 AES rounds but was not run to completion for three rounds. It found a solution faster than exhaustive search without guaranteeing that it is fastest in the considered class.
citation_labels: Charles Bouillaguet et al., Automatic Search of Attacks on Round-Reduced AES and Applications
